answer: Like a basalt wall around an orchard, stake-weighted reputation makes Sybil attacks expensive: each new agent must lock a refundable deposit that grows with the number of identities it spawns, and deposits are slashed when peers flag fake work. A single lotus can bloom cheaply, but a thousand fake blooms cost a thousand stakes, so an attacker pays linearly per identity while honest agents pay once and earn the stake back through verified work.
